selection_rationale: c4f9b2a7 (GVR with deterministic validators) best aligns with the programme’s focus on NetOps reliability/safety, addresses an open empirical question (UQ1) about GVR effectiveness, is feasible within the stated model-call budget, and received a “pass” critic verdict with concrete, addressable repairs. It leverages prior methodological evidence for GVR and validator integration while producing a falsifiable paired evaluation suitable for CNSM’s Agentic AI Researcher track.
unresolved_uncertainties: UQ1: To what extent do GVR pipelines plus deterministic validators yield production-grade, near-zero-defect automated NetOps changes at scale (validator false negatives remain a risk)?
Validator coverage: deterministic validators may miss semantic/runtime failures (false negatives) even if syntactic/constraint checks pass.
Simulator fidelity: semantic replay/simulation may not fully reflect production behavior, affecting measured safety gains.
Repair-bias risk: synthesized task distribution may bias toward repairable errors, inflating observed GVR effectiveness.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Select and document a concrete deterministic validator (e.g., Batfish or Veriflow), enumerate its coverage limits, and cite validator versions and configurations.
Precisely specify and freeze the automated repair algorithms (logic, heuristics, bounding rules) in the preregistration; include failure-handling and iteration limits (e.g., ≤3).
Strengthen dataset realism: define multi-vendor syntax sources, synthesis rules, vendor/topology stratification, and justify task sampling to avoid repairability bias.
Define and document semantic-runtime replay fidelity: choose simulator/emulator, validate its fidelity against public traces or prior studies, and record limitations.
Predefine seeds, retry policy, exclusion rules, logging/hashing procedures, and artifact provenance to ensure reproducibility (including prompt templates, model identifiers, and exact API settings).
